worked_examples.title: Risky Prowl with a mixed result
worked_examples.situation: A Lurk crosses a roofline while Bluecoat lanterns sweep the area.
worked_examples.method: Move silently across loose slate and time the crossing between patrol sweeps.
worked_examples.resolution: The Lurk reaches the balcony, but loose slate falls into the alley. The GM starts a 4-segment 'Patrol Investigates' clock with 2 ticks. The player may resist the complication with Prowess.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Controlled action that can be reconsidered
worked_examples.situation: A Spider quietly tests a clerk's willingness to accept a bribe before making the full offer.
worked_examples.goal: Learn whether the clerk can be bought.
worked_examples.method: Consort through shared contacts and indirect hints.
worked_examples.resolution: The clerk becomes wary but does not expose the Spider. The GM offers a choice: withdraw and preserve the relationship, or press the attempt from a risky position.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Desperate Wreck with full success
worked_examples.situation: A Leech is trapped beside a boiler that is seconds from rupturing.
worked_examples.goal: Vent the pressure before the room explodes.
worked_examples.method: Smash the emergency valve assembly open with heavy tools.
worked_examples.resolution: The pressure vents and the room survives. The Leech marks 1 Prowess XP because the roll was desperate.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Critical on great effect
worked_examples.situation: A Cutter with a fine heavy weapon attacks an isolated elite guard already disarmed by a setup action.
worked_examples.method: Overwhelm the guard in close combat.
worked_examples.resolution: The guard is decisively defeated and the GM may grant extreme effect or another major advantage, such as seizing the guard's access token before an alarm can be raised.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Zero-die action roll
worked_examples.situation: A Whisper with no Finesse dots tries to pick a precision lock while under fire.
worked_examples.goal: Open the lock before the shooters close in.
worked_examples.resolution: The player can improve the odds through assistance, a Devil's Bargain, or pushing before rolling. A zero-die roll cannot critical.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Resisting harm
worked_examples.situation: A Cutter suffers level-3 harm, 'Deep stab wound,' after a desperate Skirmish.
worked_examples.resolution: The table reduces the consequence according to the fiction, commonly to level-2 harm such as 'Bleeding cut.' The resistance does not erase the fact that the enemy struck.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Critical resistance
worked_examples.situation: A Slide resists being recognized by an old rival.
worked_examples.resolution: The consequence is reduced or avoided as established, and the Slide clears 1 stress instead of taking stress.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Armor and resistance are separate options
worked_examples.situation: Flying debris would cause level-2 harm during a demolition.
worked_examples.resolution: The player may mark armor if it could protect them, resist with Prowess, or use both when each produces a distinct fictional reduction and the GM agrees.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Push for a bonus die
worked_examples.situation: A Hound takes an impossible shot through smoke.
worked_examples.resolution: The Hound takes 2 stress to push for +1d. This cannot be combined with a Devil's Bargain for another bonus die on the same roll, but assistance may also add a die.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Push for increased effect
worked_examples.situation: A Cutter's ordinary blade has limited effect against a heavily armored opponent.
worked_examples.resolution: The Cutter may take 2 stress to push for increased effect, moving limited to standard if the fiction supports the attack finding a weak point.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Setup action improves a teammate
worked_examples.situation: The Spider distracts a guard captain so the Lurk can enter the records room.
worked_examples.resolution: The Spider rolls Sway as a setup. On success, the Lurk receives improved position or effect on the following infiltration, as established before the Lurk rolls.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Group action stress
worked_examples.situation: Four scoundrels Prowl across a guarded courtyard together.
worked_examples.resolution: Each rolls Prowl. The leader uses the best result for the group and takes 1 stress for each participant whose highest die is 1-3.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Protect a teammate
worked_examples.situation: A guard shoots at the Leech after a mixed Tinker result.
worked_examples.resolution: The Cutter may step into the line of fire and suffer or resist the consequence instead, provided the protection is fictionally possible.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Ordinary zero-stress flashback
worked_examples.situation: The crew reaches a servants' entrance and asks whether they previously learned the shift-change time.
worked_examples.resolution: Because this is a routine preparatory action, the GM charges 0 stress and resolves a gather-information action or states what was learned.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Complex one-stress flashback
worked_examples.situation: The Slide declares that they bribed a porter to leave a window unlatched.
worked_examples.resolution: The GM charges 1 stress because the preparation required a specific opportunity and risk, then resolves any action roll or cost required.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Elaborate two-stress flashback
worked_examples.situation: The Spider claims a replacement carriage was secretly arranged inside a secure compound.
worked_examples.resolution: The GM charges 2 or more stress and may require an action roll, coin, or a contact because the preparation is elaborate and difficult.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Engagement roll
worked_examples.situation: The crew uses a stealth plan to enter a warehouse through a roof vent identified by a contact.

disadvantages: target is alert after a recent theft

worked_examples.resolution: The score begins in a risky position at the first meaningful obstacle. The roll does not determine the entire score's success.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Acquire an asset
worked_examples.situation: A Tier 0 crew needs a trained boat pilot for one score.
worked_examples.resolution: The asset is available at quality Tier +1. Coin may boost quality further at the normal rate.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Long-term project
worked_examples.situation: The Whisper researches a ritual that conceals a room from ghosts.
worked_examples.resolution: Mark 5 ticks and describe a major breakthrough. Completion still requires all clock segments.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Recovery activity
worked_examples.situation: A physicker treats a character with level-2 harm.
worked_examples.resolution: Mark 2 healing-clock segments. When the clock fills, reduce all recorded harm one level and clear level-1 harm according to the recovery procedure.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Vice overindulgence
worked_examples.situation: A character has 2 stress and rolls a 5 while indulging vice.
worked_examples.resolution: The character clears all 2 stress but overindulges because the result exceeded current stress, then chooses or rolls an overindulgence outcome.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Heat fills and raises wanted level
worked_examples.situation: A crew at 8 heat gains 3 more heat.
worked_examples.resolution: The heat track fills, wanted level increases by 1, and excess heat carries onto the reset track according to the core procedure.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Tier changes effect, not dice difficulty
worked_examples.situation: A Tier 0 crew tries to force a Tier III vault with ordinary tools.
worked_examples.resolution: The GM does not subtract three dice. The quality gap likely produces zero or limited effect until the crew gains better tools, leverage, potency, or a different method.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

worked_examples.title: Faction status changes the next opportunity
worked_examples.situation: The crew steals a claim from the Lampblacks while secretly helping the Red Sashes.
worked_examples.resolution: Update both statuses, advance a Lampblack retaliation clock, and create a Red Sash offer that carries its own obligations.
worked_examples.source_basis: Core procedures summarized from official rules; scenario text is original.

source_mapping.original_scenarios_and_software_models: Generated synthesis grounded in the cited procedures; not official rules text.

quality_audit.benchmark_interpretation: The D&D file's size is driven partly by hundreds of spells and dozens of species. This Blades file mirrors its functional depth through complete core option catalogs, state models, validation, resolvers, and GM/player assistance rather than padding or importing irrelevant mechanics.
known_boundaries: Ability and item explanations are original summaries, not verbatim rulebook text.
The faction tracker records official names, Tier, and hold but does not reproduce every commercial-book goal, asset, quirk, and NPC.
Deep Cuts exact alternative procedures require the paid expansion.
Custom playbook and automation schemas are implementation aids rather than official game rules.

build_provenance.expansion_strategy: Retain the original guide, then add complete system-specific catalogs, engines, validation, GM support, and original worked examples.

character_creation_wizard.prompt: Choose a playbook that matches the kinds of problems you want to solve.
Choose a heritage and describe one detail that still shapes you.
Choose a background and name a former profession or institution.
Assign one action dot linked to heritage, one linked to background, and two anywhere; no action may exceed 2.
Choose one listed contact as a friend and another as a rival.
Choose a vice and identify the purveyor, place, or practice.
Choose a name, alias, and look, then calculate attributes.
Review stress, trauma, harm, armor, coin, stash, load, XP tracks, and item lists.

action_choice_helper.question: Are you mainly moving through danger or concealment?
Are you tracking or attacking from prepared range?
Are you observing the whole situation?
Are you analyzing a specific detail, person, or mystery?
Are you modifying or bypassing a mechanism?
Are you using precision handling or vehicle control?
Are you fighting directly at close range?
Are you destroying or forcing something?
Are you interacting with the ghost field?
Are you compelling through authority or fear?
Are you relying on relationships or shared community?
Are you persuading, deceiving, or manipulating?

nonbinding_guidance: Pushing is more attractive when one die sharply reduces the chance of a 1-3 result or when increased effect is necessary for the goal to be possible.
Assistance shifts stress to a teammate and requires them to describe how they help.
A Devil's Bargain adds a die without stress but its cost happens regardless of the roll.
At high stress, consider setup actions, equipment, altered approach, or accepting consequences instead of automatically pushing.
Resistance is decided after a consequence is known, so preserve some stress capacity for severe consequences.
stress_advisor.authority_note: This advisor never chooses for the player and should not hide risks or expected costs.

harm_penalty_reminders.level_1: Reduced effect when the harm interferes.
harm_penalty_reminders.level_3: The character needs help to act when the harm interferes.
harm_penalty_reminders.level_4: Fatal unless prevented or altered immediately.
harm_penalty_reminders.application_rule: Apply a harm penalty only when the described action is actually hindered by that harm.

session_end_prompt: Did you address a challenge using your playbook's characteristic approach?
Did you express beliefs, drives, heritage, or background?
Did you struggle with vice or trauma?
Did the crew complete its crew-specific operation type?
Did the crew contend with challenges above its current station?
Did the crew bolster its reputation or develop a new one?
Did the crew express goals, drives, inner conflict, or essential nature?
